narrative:
The model estimates a 51% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the organization has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned about investing in someone who may not stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by your relatively short overall work experience. Most employees the model expects to stay have been working for six years or longer, while you fall into the 1-5 year category. This lack of broader experience is the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Your access to other job opportunities also pushes the model in the same direction, as having external offers often signals that someone is considering a move. Finally, the time you have spent in your current role adds a smaller but still noticeable influence toward leaving, since most employees the model sees as likely to stay have been with their organization longer than five years.

Taken together, these three factors outweigh the many positive aspects of your situation, such as having medical insurance, benefiting from training, and receiving a reasonable salary for your experience level.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether you see a long-term future here and what would make staying more appealing. Addressing these points early could change the outlook for both sides. (218 words)
